payload.claim: `RebutResult.as_dict()` is documented as the sole record of verdict detail ("the ledger has no `findings` table, so `verdict` ... have nowhere to go but this artifact", line 103-104), it is written to `rebuttal.json` in the task directory (`saffron/cell/session.py:2747-2748`), and `saffron/report/pr_body.py` explicitly points the operator at that file ("see `rebuttal.json`", lines 303 and 560) for verdict detail. The per-lens dict built here (lines 117-125) serializes `lens`, `error`, `cost_usd` and `verdicts` but omits the new `LensVerdicts.never_started` flag this change adds specifically to distinguish an infrastructure fault (routes to `GATE_ERROR`) from an ordinary unjudged-verdict error (routes to `REBUTTING`). Anyone reading the persisted artifact after the fact — rather than the live object `pr_body.py` happens to still hold in memory — cannot tell a never-started verdict session from any other errored one; the fact only survives in the free-text top-level `why` string.
